answer: A good way to blunt sybil attacks is to make identity costly before an agent can earn anything. Imagine a marketplace where a new agent, call her Sparrow, must stake a small deposit and have an existing peer vouch for her; when a gale of fake agents hits, each one burns that stake the moment it cheats, while vouches decay unless renewed. A veteran agent like Quill only signs attestations for identities it can monitor, so forgery becomes expensive and reputation propagates through a web of real accountability rather than free pseudonyms.
